subject: english-language
title: Commas, Colons, Semicolons
welcome_lead: Mid-sentence marks shape meaning and pace.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on commas, colons and semicolons.
final_note: You can now use commas, colons and semicolons correctly.

concepts.def: Pair of commas around extra info.

walkthroughs.body_html: Use listing commas: 'apples, pears, plums'. Use bracketing commas around extra info: 'My uncle, the doctor, agreed.'
A colon introduces ('You need: bread, jam, butter.'). A semicolon joins two related sentences ('I was tired; I went home.').
Apostrophes show missing letters ('don't') or possession ('Tom's bag'). Don't use them for normal plurals.
